definitions.gloss: spitting image; very much alike; like two peas in a pod
definitions.explanation: Describes two people or things that look extremely similar, especially in physical appearance. Derives from the idea that when you cut a melon ({瓜|うり}) in half, the two halves look identical.

examples.japanese: ⟦{親子|おやこ}→親子：10430_oyako⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つだ。
examples.english: The parent and child are the spitting image of each other.

examples.japanese: ⟦{双子|ふたご}→双子：03599_futago⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姉妹|しまい}→姉妹：03201_shimai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つで{見分|みわ}け⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つかない。
examples.english: The twin sisters look so alike that you can't tell them apart.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{写真|しゃしん}→写真：00753_shashin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}たら→見る：00283_miru⟧、⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つで⟦{驚|おどろ}いた→驚く：01255_odoroku⟧。
examples.english: When I saw a photo of my mother when she was young, I was surprised at how much she looked like my daughter.

notes:
The etymology comes from cutting a ⟦{瓜|うり}→瓜：13597_uri⟧ (gourd/melon) in half — the two halves are perfectly identical. This is one of the most common expressions for describing a strong family resemblance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つだ — to be the spitting image
- ⟦{父親|ちちおや}→父親：03469_chichioya⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ — the spitting image of one's father
- ⟦まるで→まるで：03739_marude⟧{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ — exactly alike

USAGE:
Most often used to describe resemblance between family members, especially parent and child. Can also be used for unrelated people who happen to look very similar. Typically used as a predicate with だ or ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦そっくり→そっくり：00378_sokkuri⟧ — looking just like (more casual and broadly used; {瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ is more vivid and literary)
- {生|い}き{写|うつ}し — a living copy (more literary; emphasizes an almost uncanny resemblance)
